{{Short description|System of units used for N-body simulations}}
{{DISPLAYTITLE:''N''-body units}} 
{| class="wikitable" align="right" style="margin-left: 1em;"
! Quantity
! Expression
|- align="left"
| Unit of [[length]] (''R'')
| <math>\frac{1}{R} = \frac{1}{M^2} \sum_{i,j \ne i}^{N} \frac{m_i m_j}{\left| \vec{r_j}-\vec{r_i} \right| }</math>
|-
| Unit of [[mass]] (''M'')
| <math>M = \sum_{i=1}^{N} m_i</math>
|}
<!--
:<math> M =  G =  R = 1 \ </math>
-->
'''''N''-body units''' are a completely self-contained [[Systems of measurement|system of units]] used for [[N-body simulation|''N''-body simulation]]s of self-gravitating systems in astrophysics. In this system, the base physical units are chosen so that the total mass, ''M'', the [[gravitational constant]], ''G'', and the [[virial radius]], ''R'', are normalized. The underlying assumption is that the system of ''N'' objects (stars) satisfies the [[virial theorem]]. The consequence of standard ''N''-body units is that the velocity dispersion of the system, ''v'', is <math> \scriptstyle \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{2} </math> and that the dynamical or crossing time, ''t'', is <math> \scriptstyle 2\sqrt{2} </math>.
The use of standard ''N''-body units was advocated by [[Michel Hénon]] in 1971.<ref>{{cite journal | last = Hénon | first = Michel | author-link = Michel Hénon
 | title = The Monte Carlo Method | journal = Astrophysics and Space Science
 | volume = 14 | issue = 1 
 | pages = 151–167 | date = 1971
 | doi = 10.1007/BF00649201 | bibcode=1971Ap&SS..14..151H| s2cid = 115854730 }}</ref> Early adopters of this system of units included H. Cohn in 1979<ref>{{cite journal | last = Cohn | first = Haldan | title = Numerical integration of the Fokker-Planck equation and the evolution of star clusters | journal = The Astrophysical Journal | volume = 234| pages = 1036–1053 | date = 1979
 | doi = 10.1086/157587 | bibcode=1979ApJ...234.1036C| doi-access = free }}</ref> and D. Heggie and R. Mathieu in 1986.<ref>{{cite book | title = The Use of Supercomputers in Stellar Dynamics | chapter = Standardised units and time scales | bibcode = 1986LNP...267..233H | doi = 10.1007/BFb0116419 | series = [[Lecture Notes in Physics]] | volume = 267 | date = 1986 | pages = 233–235 | first1 = D. C. | last1 = Heggie | first2 = R. D. | last2 = Mathieu | editor1-first = P. | editor1-last = Hut | editor2-first = S. | editor2-last = McMillan | isbn = 978-3-540-17196-6 }}</ref> At the conference [http://www.astro.uni-bonn.de/~sambaran/DS2014/ MODEST14] in 2014, D. Heggie proposed that the community abandon the name "''N''-body units" and replace it with the name "Hénon units" to commemorate the originator.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.astro.uni-bonn.de/~sambaran/DS2014/Modest14_Talks/Heggie.pdf|title=Escape from isolated, equal-mass star clusters|author=Douglas C. Heggie|location=[[University of Edinburgh]]|date=3 June 2014|website=Astro.uni-bonn.de|access-date=30 November 2017}}</ref>
